_comment-scribe-pvp-verb: Weapon-aware PvP kill verbs, resolved in 3 tiers (ScribeModSystem.ResolvePvpVerb): (1) pvp-verb-tool-<EnumTool name, lowercased> off the killer's held item; (2) pvp-verb-damage-<EnumDamageType name, lowercased> off the damage source; (3) the pvp-verb-generic-N pool, chosen with no immediate repeat. A missing tier-1/2 key falls through to the next tier, so only add keys for categories you want a specific verb for.
_comment-scribe-pvp-verb-generic: Generic no-repeat pool. Keys MUST be contiguous from -0; the pool size is discovered by probing upward until a key is missing, so don't leave a gap.
_comment-scribe-pvp-verb-participle: Passive participle overrides for the victim-first death message ('{victim} was <participle> by {killer}'). A verb whose passive participle differs from its active past tense needs an override keyed '<verb-key>-participle'; when absent, the active verb is reused (correct for 'shot'/'slashed'/'bashed'/etc., which are identical either way). Only 'slew' → 'slain' differs in the shipped English set. The kill message ('{killer} <verb> {victim}') always uses the active verb, never the participle.
_comment-scribe-pvp-message: Two forms of the same PvP event, each written from its own notebook owner's perspective. The victim's Death log uses the victim-first passive 'death' form ({0}=victim, {1}=passive participle, {2}=killer). The killer's PvpKill log uses the killer-first active 'kill' form ({0}=killer, {1}=active verb, {2}=victim). Keep both {0}/{1}/{2} placeholders in any translation.
_comment-scribe-mob-death: Flavored messages for being killed by a creature (not another player). {0} = victim name, {1} = the creature named as an object phrase (e.g. 'a nightmare drifter', 'a brown bear'), taken from the entity's own GetPrefixAndCreatureName so it is always the correct variant. Chosen at random from a contiguous pool: keys MUST run from -0 with no gap (the pool size is discovered by probing upward until a key is missing). Translators may ship as few as one (just -0) — add or remove trailing entries freely.
scribe-mob-death-6: {0} met a grisly end at the claws of {1}.
scribe-mob-death-9: {0} picked a fight with {1} and lost.
_comment-scribe-death-fallback: Defensive fallbacks used by BuildDeathMessage only when no scribe-mob-death-* or vanilla deathmsg-* key matched (normally unreachable, since the mod ships those keys). {0} = victim name, {1} = the creature phrase.
_comment-scribe-date-format: In-game calendar date shown in History entries, the Lectern Guest Book, and item tooltips. {0} = day of month, {1} = localized month name, {2} = year. Reorder the parts and translate the word 'Year' freely.

handbook-scribelectern-about-text:
The Lectern is Scribe's shared, placed writing surface — a fixed block anyone can walk up to and use. rightmouse to open it in Read view; Shift+secondarymouse quick-adds a fresh & editable task at the top. Unlike Scribe's carried items, a Lectern stays put, is readable by everyone, merely guards editing with a one-at-a-time editor lock, and keeps a public Guest Book of its visitors.

For keyboard shortcuts and text-editing mechanics see Scribe Mod: Editor Reference, and for an overview of the whole mod see Scribe Mod: Getting Started.
handbook-scribelectern-views-text:
The Lectern has Read, Task Editor, Pinned, Guest Book, and Settings tabs, switched via the icon buttons in the right-hand sidebar. Being a shared, placed block, its Guest Book is public — a log of everyone who visits, each with the date of their visit and an optional short message — and only one player may edit it at a time.

For what each tab does, see Scribe Mod: Tabs & Views.
handbook-scriptorium-about-text:
The word scriptorium comes from the monastic writing rooms where scribes copied manuscripts by hand — and copying is what sets this block apart. The Scriptorium is Scribe's dedicated shared, placed writing station — like the Lectern, a fixed block anyone can walk up to and use — but it is also the one place you can copy, merge, import, and export whole documents between Scribe items, from its Transcribe tab. rightmouse to open it in Read view; Shift+secondarymouse quick-adds a fresh & editable task at the top. It stays put, is readable by everyone, guards editing with a one-at-a-time editor lock, and keeps a public Guest Book of its visitors.

For keyboard shortcuts and text-editing mechanics see Scribe Mod: Editor Reference, and for an overview of the whole mod see Scribe Mod: Getting Started.
handbook-scriptorium-views-text:
The Scriptorium has the same tabs as the Lectern — Read, Task Editor, Pinned, Guest Book, and Settings — plus the one tab that sets it apart:

Transcribe — the copy desk. Drop a Scribe item into a slot and duplicate or append its tasks onto another, or move a whole document through your clipboard as JSON or TSV to back it up, share it, or edit it in a spreadsheet. See Scribe Mod: The Transcribe Tab for the details.

For what the shared tabs do, see Scribe Mod: Tabs & Views.
handbook-chalkboard-about-text:
The Chalkboard is the Lectern in a different frame: the same shared, placed writing surface, but hung on a wall like a painting rather than stood on the floor. Point at a wall and place it to mount it facing outward. rightmouse to open it in Read view; Shift+secondarymouse quick-adds a fresh & editable task at the top. Like the Lectern it stays put, is readable by everyone, guards editing with a one-at-a-time editor lock, and keeps a public Guest Book of its visitors.

For keyboard shortcuts and text-editing mechanics see Scribe Mod: Editor Reference, and for an overview of the whole mod see Scribe Mod: Getting Started.
handbook-scribe-hud-ref-text: Pin any task to keep it on your always-on Pinned Task HUD over the game world — see Scribe Mod: The Pinned Task HUD for how it works.
craftinginfo-scribe-getting-started-text:
Welcome to Scribe
Scribe is a mod to help you keep track of what you want to do. Use Scribe to write tasks and notes, to pin them to a persistent HUD, or to enrich your experiences with other players.

How do I start?
Scribe features a number of blocks and items you craft:
Clay Tablets — a slate you carry. The first thing you can make in Scribe. A simple, limited manager for tasks. Dries and hardens, but can be softened again with water.
Wax Tablet — a more reliable tablet. Requires a saw, but is still limited.
Lectern — a placed block. Shared and readable by everyone, with an editor lock and a Guestbook.
Chalkboard — the same tabs as a Lectern, mounted on a wall like a painting.
Scriptorium — a dedicated shared writing station, the collaborative hub of a settlement.
Notebook — a personal, carried document that travels in your inventory and keeps its own History chronicle.
Clockmaker's Notebook — a Notebook with an added countdown Timer.

Using Scribe
Scribe is meant to be easy to use. When holding a Scribe item, press rightmouse to open it. For the Tablet, you can then click the "Add Task" button or press Enter to create one. You can delete the task, pin it to your HUD, or change it in the order. More details are on the Scribe Mod: Editor Reference in the handbook.

The views
More advanced Scribe items (Notebooks, Lecterns) have advanced and multiple views.
Read: scroll, complete, and pin tasks to your HUD.
Task Editor: also add, edit, reorder, and delete rows. On a Lectern, one player edits at a time.
Pinned: all your pins across every Lectern and Notebook, editable in place.
Settings: all Scribe preferences.
Other: Guest Book (Lectern, Scriptorium, and Chalkboard), History (Notebook), Timer (Clockmaker's Notebook)
For a full tour of every tab, see Scribe Mod: Tabs & Views.

Task types
Beyond plain tasks and notes, Scribe has three item-bound task types: Item Trackers (a live have / need count of items you're carrying), Links (a quick handbook cross-reference), and Crafting Tasks (a recipe-bound goal that builds an ingredient shopping list). All three are added from an item's own handbook page. See Scribe Mod: Item Trackers, Links & Crafting Tasks.

Pinned task HUD
Pin any task to keep it on an always-on overlay over the game world. See Scribe Mod: The Pinned Task HUD for how pinning, checking off, and collapsing the HUD work.

Assignments and quests
Hand a task directly to another player from an Assignment Desk, and receive one in your own or a standalone Inbox. See Scribe Mod: Assignments & the Inbox. If you also play with a quest mod, Scribe can link and even auto-track its quests too — see Scribe Mod: Quest Links.
craftinginfo-scribe-pinned-hud-title: Scribe Mod: The Pinned Task HUD
craftinginfo-scribe-pinned-hud-text:
The Pinned Task HUD is an always-on overlay that shows your pinned tasks over the game world, so the things you're tracking stay in view without opening any Scribe item.

Pinning tasks
Hover a task row in Read or Task Editor view and click the pin icon to add it to your HUD. Pins are per-player — pinning a task on a shared Lectern only affects your own HUD, never anyone else's. Your pins are gathered across every Scribe item you use (Tablets, Notebooks, and Lecterns) and are all listed together in the Pinned tab, editable in place.

Item Trackers, Links, and Crafting Tasks
You can pin Item Tracker, Link, and Crafting Task rows too: a pinned Item Tracker or Crafting Task shows its live have / need count right on the HUD, and clicking a pinned Link opens its handbook page. See Scribe Mod: Item Trackers, Links & Crafting Tasks.

Checking tasks off
Checking off a task from the HUD starts a 1.5-second undo window. During that window the task text fades as a countdown, and unchecking cancels the action entirely. After the window elapses the completion is applied according to your chosen policy — keep pinned, unpin, sink to bottom, or delete the task. The same policies apply to tasks you complete inside a Lectern or Notebook.

Collapsing the HUD
Press scribepinhud (rebindable under Controls: Scribe Mod) or click the Pinned header to shrink the HUD to just its header. You can also start it collapsed with Collapse the HUD in Scribe Settings.

Overflow
The HUD shows a limited number of rows at once (set by Max HUD rows, 1–10, in Settings). When you have more pins than that, the extras are summarized as a "+N more" line at the bottom.

Position and size
Everything about the HUD's placement lives in Scribe Settings: HUD position picks the screen corner or edge it anchors to, HUD offset nudges it from there, HUD task width sets how wide each row is, and HUD text size scales the text.

Timers
A running Clockmaker's Notebook timer also appears on the HUD, counting down; when it finishes it blinks and rocks to get your attention.

Temporal storms
During a temporal storm — or when your stability drops low — the HUD scrambles its text and its title reads "Survive the Storm". Turn off Storm corruption in Settings to keep it fully legible.
craftinginfo-scribe-editor-reference-tex:
Editor Features
The following functionality is available anywhere you can edit tasks in Scribe items. Note that all typing is autosaved, don't worry about hitting escapemenudialog.

Many of the following keys are hardcoded and cannot be modified or remapped.

Row navigation
Tab — move to the next row.
Shift+Tab — move to the previous row.
Cmd+Up (macOS) or Ctrl+Up / Ctrl+Home (Windows) — jump to the first row.
Cmd+Down or Ctrl+Down / Ctrl+End — jump to the last row.
Enter — insert a new empty task.
Shift+Enter — insert a hard line break within the current row.
Esc — commit and close the Lectern.

Caret movement
Arrow keys — move one character or line.
Alt/Option+Left/Right — skip by whole word.
Cmd+Left/Right (macOS) or Home/End — jump to line start or end.
Ctrl+Left/Right (Windows) — skip by whole word.
Hold Shift with any movement key to extend the selection.

Selection and clipboard
Ctrl/Cmd+A — select all text in the focused field.
Ctrl/Cmd+C — copy. Ctrl/Cmd+X — cut. Ctrl/Cmd+V — paste.
Typing while text is selected replaces the selection.

Adding tasks
Add Task button — at the bottom of the Editor.
Enter — inserts a task directly below the current row. Both create an empty row ready to type into immediately.
Quick-add (Shift+secondarymouse a Lectern, Notebook, or wet Tablet) — opens the editor with a fresh empty task at the TOP of the list, caret ready.
Item Trackers, Links, and Crafting Tasks — these handbook-created types are added from an item's own handbook page, not the Add button. See Scribe Mod: Item Trackers, Links & Crafting Tasks. Tap the row's drag grip (without holding to reorder) to indent it as a subtask, or tap again to promote it.

Empty task behaviour
When you move focus away from a task row (Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Esc, or clicking elsewhere), that row is Saved. However, empty rows are deleted. An empty row that still has focus is not deleted.

On commit, trailing blank lines and trailing whitespace are trimmed from a non-empty row. Interior line breaks (from Shift+Enter) are preserved.
craftinginfo-scribe-views-text:
Most Scribe surfaces share the same set of tabs, switched via the icon buttons in the right-hand sidebar. Which tabs appear depends on the surface — a placed block, a carried item, or the Scriptorium.

Read — see all tasks and notes as a scrollable list. Read, pin, and check off tasks from here.
Task Editor — full document editing: add tasks, edit text, pin rows, reorder by drag, and delete rows. Changes autosave as you type. On a shared placed surface, only one player may edit at a time.
Pinned — all of your pinned tasks, gathered from every Scribe item you use, editable in place.
Settings — opens the Scribe Settings panel (the same panel as the gear icon on the Pinned Task HUD).

Tabs that depend on the surface
Guest Book — on placed surfaces: the Lectern, the Scriptorium, and the Chalkboard. A public log of who has visited, each recorded with the date of their visit and an optional short message. Because a placed block is shared, its Guest Book is meant to be seen by everyone who opens it.
History — on carried items: the Notebook and Clockmaker's Notebook. A private, per-item chronicle that fills in automatically and travels with the item — the personal counterpart to the shared Guest Book.
Transcribe and Import / Export — only on the Scriptorium, the one place you can copy, merge, import, and export whole documents between Scribe items. See Scribe Mod: The Transcribe Tab.
Timer — only on the Clockmaker's Notebook, a single countdown that shows on your Pinned Task HUD.

For keyboard shortcuts and text-editing mechanics, see Scribe Mod: Editor Reference.
craftinginfo-scribe-transcribe-text:
The Transcribe tab on the Scriptorium copies the writing from one Scribe item onto another — a way to duplicate a checklist, hand out copies of a plan, or back up a Notebook onto a Tablet.

Copying
Place the item you want to copy FROM in the Copy from slot, and the item you want to copy INTO in the Paste into slot. Both slots accept only Scribe items (Notebooks, Tablets, and picked-up Lecterns or Scriptoriums). Press Copy and the source's tasks and notes are written onto the target, replacing whatever it held.

The two documents are fully independent afterward: editing one never changes the other. The source is left untouched — only the target is overwritten.

Overwriting
If the Paste into item already has tasks, the first press of Copy turns red and warns how many tasks it will overwrite; press it a second time to confirm. Changing either slot cancels the pending confirmation. Copying onto an empty item happens immediately, with no confirm.

When you can't copy
Copy is disabled (greyed) until both slots hold a Scribe item and the target can accept the copy. A hardened or fired Tablet can't be written to. A Tablet also has a task limit, so a source with more tasks than the target can hold is refused. The button's tooltip explains which rule is blocking it.

Import / Export
The lower half of the tab moves a Scribe document through your system clipboard as plain text — for backing a list up, sharing it, or editing it in another program. Place a Scribe item in the Import / Export slot, then:

There are two lanes, for two jobs. JSON is the exact lane — a complete, lossless copy, best for backing a list up or moving it between items untouched. TSV is the forgiving lane — a spreadsheet-friendly table (like CSV) that's easy to edit by hand and shrugs off small mistakes on the way back in, at the cost of a little detail. Reach for JSON when you want the document preserved exactly; reach for TSV when you want to edit it.

Copy as JSON writes the exact copy to the clipboard. Paste it into a plain-text editor — Notepad++ on Windows or CotEditor on macOS — rather than a word processor, which can silently "fix" quotes or spacing and break the import. Save or share the text, then Import it back later.

Copy as TSV writes a tab-separated table — paste it straight into a spreadsheet (Excel, Google Sheets) to see one row per task under the columns Type, Done, Text, Special, Count, Depth. Edit the text or an item tracker's count, copy the rows back, and Import them.

Import reads the clipboard, figures out on its own whether it's JSON or TSV, and writes it onto the slotted item using the Overwrite / Append choice above — Overwrite replaces the item's tasks (with the same red two-press confirm as Copy when it isn't empty), Append adds them after the existing ones. A tracker or link whose item isn't found in this game is imported as a plain task instead, and a message tells you how many. Anything on the clipboard that isn't a Scribe export is rejected with no change.

Imported tasks are always unpinned — importing never touches your pins, in this world or any other.
craftinginfo-scribe-assignments-text:
Assignment Desk
The Assignment Desk block is the only place to hand a task directly to another player. Its Assignment tab is a create/send form: write the task text and pick a player, and Send creates the assignment. Once sent, that same tab keeps showing you the assignment's current state (Accepted, later auto-Completed) as a read-only record of what you sent — the action buttons disappear once it's out of your hands, but the record itself never does.

Inbox
Assignments you receive land in an Inbox — either the standalone Inbox block (receiving only, no create form), or the Inbox tab available from the Assignment Desk, Lectern, Scriptorium, and Chalkboard via a nav button. Every Inbox surface shows the same rows: a checkbox/tracker, the task text, a depth indent for subtasks, and a compact state chip. Click the chevron at a row's leading edge to expand it for the assigner's name, the in-game date it was sent, and whatever action buttons apply to you right now. A row of filter chips above the list lets you show any combination of the six states at once.

States
An assignment moves through a small, one-way set of states: Unaccepted (just arrived — you can Accept or Decline; the sender can still Cancel) → Accepted (yours now — the sender's cancel window has closed) → Completed (automatic the moment you check the task off — there is no separate "mark complete" button). Declining, Cancelling, or Discarding an Accepted task instead ends it in Declined, Cancelled, or Discarded. Every one of those is final — retrying is always a brand-new assignment, never a revived old one.

Accepting a task
Accepting places the task into a Scribe item: whichever one you're currently holding, or (if your hands are empty) one from your inventory — you'll be asked to pick if you're carrying more than one. If you're carrying no Scribe item at all, Accept is disabled until you are. Once accepted, the task's text is fixed (it came from the sender, not you), but its checkbox, pin, and place in your document all work exactly like any other task — including Delete, which for an accepted assignment performs the Discard transition rather than a plain removal, so the sender's record always matches what you actually did.

Noticing new assignments
An unseen assignment glows softly on every Inbox-capable block nearby until you open that block's Inbox and see it.
craftinginfo-scribe-quests-text:
This page only applies if you also have a compatible quest mod installed (currently VS Quest or Progression Framework, the framework behind mods like Seafarer). Without either one, Scribe's quest features are simply not present anywhere in the mod. With both installed, Quest Links from each show up together, and each Link always tracks against the one mod it actually came from.

Quest Links
A Quest Link is a Link row that points at one of that mod's quests instead of a Handbook page. Create one from the footer's New Task dropdown: pick Quest Link, then choose the quest from the list that opens in its place. Like any Link, it isn't a task — no checkbox, doesn't count against a tablet's limit — it's a reminder that sits next to your other goals with the quest's title and description captured at the moment you added it. If the quest mod is later uninstalled, the Link still shows that captured text; it just stops updating.

Automatic detection
Scribe also quietly notices when you accept or complete a quest, and always tells you so in chat — this isn't hidden, even if you've told it to do nothing. What happens next follows two settings in Scribe Settings, each Always/Never/Prompt (default Prompt):
Quest Accept Policy — Always creates a Quest Link for the newly-accepted quest automatically, added to whichever Notebook or Tablet you're carrying (if you're carrying more than one, it asks which); Never does nothing; Prompt shows you a small banner on the pinned-task HUD so you can choose, with the same destination choice if needed.
Quest Completion Policy — the same three choices, but for marking an already-pinned Quest Link's task done the moment Scribe notices the quest itself is complete.

Live progress
For a VS Quest Link: while that quest's own dialog is open, the read view shows a live count of any kill/place/break objectives underneath it (gathering-type objectives aren't tracked this way — the quest mod itself has no running count for those, only Scribe's static Link). For a Progression Framework Link: progress shows automatically, with no dialog needed — a single-objective quest shows its status, and a multi-objective one (e.g. a delivery quest with several items) shows how many of its objectives are complete.
craftinginfo-scribe-task-types-text:
Besides plain Tasks and Notes, Scribe has three task types that are tied to a specific item or recipe. All three are created the same way: open that item's handbook page, scroll to the bottom, and click Add Item Tracker, Add Link, or Add Crafting Task under the "Add to Scribe" heading. They can't be added from the editor's Add button, because they need to know which item (and which recipe) you mean.

Item Tracker
A Item Tracker is a task bound to an item that shows a live have / need count, following the items you're carrying. For example, a item tracker for 20 iron ingots reads 12/20 while you carry twelve and completes on its own once you have all twenty. Set the target amount with the row's up/down stepper. Item Trackers count as tasks, so they share the tablet's task limit.

Link
A Link is a row whose label opens the linked item's handbook page when you click it — a quick cross-reference to keep next to a task ("see: forge"). Links aren't tasks: they have no checkbox and don't count against the task limit. Cooked-meal handbook pages offer Add Link too, so a stew or pie can sit next to your other goals.

Crafting Task
A Crafting Task is a goal bound to one of an item's grid recipes. It tracks the output like an Item Tracker, and it builds a shopping list of ingredient subtasks underneath — one Item Tracker per ingredient, at the quantity the batch needs. If the item has more than one recipe variant, the handbook page offers a labeled link for each. Liquid ingredients are tracked in litres. Completing the output uses the same Tracker completion setting as Item Trackers.

Where it lands
Clicking Add Item Tracker, Add Link, or Add Crafting Task adds the row to whichever Scribe surface you have open. If none is open, it's added to the Scribe item you most recently used (or the first one you're carrying). If you have no Scribe item at all, you'll be told you need one first.
item-scribenotebook-desc: A personal notebook. Write tasks and notes anywhere.
item-scribeclockmakernotebook-desc: A notebook with a built-in timer. Set countdowns in real or in-game time.
item-clockmakerschematic-desc: A trader's blueprint. Lets anyone craft a Clockmaker's Notebook, no Clockmaker class needed. Not used up when crafting.
item-scribetablet-clay-red-desc: A simple early-game writing surface. Scratch a short list of tasks and notes into the red clay.
item-scribetablet-clay-blue-desc: A simple early-game writing surface. Scratch a short list of tasks and notes into the blue clay.
item-scribetablet-clay-fire-desc: A simple early-game writing surface. Scratch a short list of tasks and notes into the fire clay.
item-scribetablet-clay-red-hard-desc: A red clay tablet dried hard. It can no longer be written on until softened again in water.
item-scribetablet-clay-blue-hard-desc: A blue clay tablet dried hard. It can no longer be written on until softened again in water.
item-scribetablet-clay-fire-hard-desc: A fire clay tablet dried hard. It can no longer be written on until softened again in water.
item-scribetablet-clay-red-fired-desc: A red clay tablet fired hard in a fire. Its writing is now permanent and can no longer be changed.
item-scribetablet-clay-blue-fired-desc: A blue clay tablet fired hard in a fire. Its writing is now permanent and can no longer be changed.
item-scribetablet-clay-fire-fired-desc: A fire clay tablet fired hard in a fire. Its writing is now permanent and can no longer be changed.
item-scribetablet-wax-desc: A reusable writing surface, a small step up from clay. Scratch a short list of tasks and notes into the wax.
handbook-scribetablet-about-text:
The clay Tablet is the earliest Scribe writing surface — cheap to craft long before a Notebook or Lectern. secondarymouse while holding it to open its tasks and notes; Shift+secondarymouse quick-adds a new task at the top.

It's deliberately limited: up to 10 tasks and one pinned task — a quick scratchpad, not a full journal.
handbook-scribetablet-states-text: A fresh clay Tablet is wet — free to write and edit. Left alone, it dries hard over about two days, locking its writing. From there, dunk it in water to soften it back to wet, or fire it in a fire pit to make its writing permanent.
handbook-scribetablet-hard-text:
This clay Tablet has dried hard — its tasks and notes are locked. You can still take it either way:

• Dunk it in water (drop it into a water block, or wade in while holding it) to soften it back to a wet, editable Tablet. This also resets its drying timer.
• Fire it in a fire pit to make its writing permanent.
handbook-scribetablet-fired-text: This clay Tablet has been fired hard — its tasks and notes are now permanent, and water won't soften it, unlike a merely hardened one. Fire a Tablet to preserve a list for good: place a wet or hardened clay Tablet in a fire pit and light it, just like firing pottery.
handbook-scribetablet-wax-text:
A small step up from the clay Tablet: a wooden frame filled with beeswax. It never dries or fires, so it can always be rewritten. secondarymouse while holding it to open its tasks and notes; Shift+secondarymouse quick-adds a new task at the top.

Same limits as the clay Tablet — up to 10 tasks and one pinned task.
handbook-scribenotebook-about-text: The Notebook is a personal, carried version of the Lectern. secondarymouse while holding it to open your own document of tasks and notes. Shift+secondarymouse quick-adds a new task at the top.
handbook-scribenotebook-editor-text:
The Notebook uses the same editor as the Lectern, but as a carried item it has no Guest Book — instead it keeps a private History chronicle. Its tabs are Read, Task Editor, Pinned, and History.

For what each tab does, see Scribe Mod: Tabs & Views; for keyboard shortcuts and text-editing mechanics, see Scribe Mod: Editor Reference.
handbook-scribenotebook-history-text:
Every notebook keeps a private History chronicle on its History tab — a newest-first log that fills in automatically as you carry it. Recorded events include when it was Crafted, who Picked it up, your Deaths, players you Killed, Bosses defeated, and Temporal Storms weathered while it with on you.

History is per-notebook and travels with the item, so each notebook tells the story of its own owner. This is unlike the Lectern's public Guest Book tab, which logs visitors to a shared block.
handbook-scribenotebook-craft-text: Once you have a Notebook you can upgrade it into a Clockmaker's Notebook, retaining your tasks and History, but adding the Timer feature.
handbook-scribeclockmakernotebook-about-: The Clockmaker's Notebook adds a Timer to everything the Notebook does: carried tasks, notes, pins, and history.
handbook-scribeclockmakernotebook-timer-:
Open the Timer tab to set a single countdown with an optional label and a duration in hours, minutes, and seconds. Choose Real time (counts down in real-world seconds) or In-game time (counts down in game-world time, which runs faster). The timer belongs to you, it runs as long as you're online, and its countdown shows on your Pinned Task HUD.

When it reaches zero, the HUD timer blinks and its icon rocks back and forth to get your attention. By default the finished timer disappears from the HUD after about 30 seconds; you can also clear it early by clicking the HUD timer or pressing Stop Timer in the Clockmaker's Notebook.

If you would rather the timer stay until you manually dismiss it, turn off Timer disappears in Scribe Settings — the finished timer then remains on the HUD until you click it or press Stop Timer.
handbook-scribeclockmakernotebook-craft-:
Requires the Tinkerer trait. By default only players of the Clockmaker class (which grants the Tinkerer trait) can craft it; if the recipe will not complete for you, that is why. A server operator can lift this requirement for everyone by running /worldconfig scribeClockmakerRequiresTrait false and then restarting the world or server.

No Clockmaker class? Wandering Commodities and Treasure Hunter traders occasionally sell a Clockmaker's Notebook Schematic.
handbook-clockmakerschematic-about-text:
A trader's blueprint, used to craft a Clockmaker's Notebook from a Notebook
with other ingredients — no Clockmaker character class or Tinkerer trait required. The schematic is a reusable blueprint: it is not consumed by the craft. It is sold occasionally by wandering Commodities and Treasure Hunter traders.
scribe-gui-inventory-empty: This storage holds Scribe items — Notebooks, Tablets, and picked-up Lecterns or Scriptoriums.
